title_en: 275: How Geopolitics Is Redefining Defense, Energy, Technology and Global Markets
title_zh: 275：地缘政治如何重新定义国防、能源、科技与全球市场
subtitle_zh: BlackRock 地缘政治研究与策略团队的 Anna Parker 与主题策略投资组合经理 Yasmin Meissner 做客 The Bid，解析竞争、碎片化与一连串冲击如何推动全球经济转向韧性经济（resilience economy），并拆解能源、国防与人工智能三大支柱下的战略咽喉节点、供应链依赖，以及对投资组合的真正含义。
description: 275: How Geopolitics Is Redefining Defense, Energy, Technology and Global Markets

turns.en: Geopolitical tensions are increasingly reshaping the global economy. Defense spending is rising, energy security has moved back up the policy agenda, and competition over artificial intelligence and critical technologies is becoming an important part of national security. At the same time, conflicts and supply chain disruptions
turns.zh: 地缘政治紧张局势正在日益重塑全球经济。国防开支不断攀升，能源安全重新回到政策议程的靠前位置，围绕人工智能（AI）和关键技术的竞争正在成为国家安全的重要组成部分。与此同时，冲突和供应链中断

turns.en: are exposing just how interconnected and in some cases vulnerable, the global system has become. So what does this changing geopolitical landscape mean for markets and investors? The headlines tend to focus on volatility, shock, churn, chaos in the environment, but that's really not the most important theme for investors to focus on.
turns.zh: 正在暴露出全球体系已经变得多么相互关联，在某些方面又多么脆弱。那么，这种不断变化的地缘政治格局对市场和投资者意味着什么？新闻头条往往聚焦于波动、冲击、翻搅、环境中的混乱，但那其实并不是投资者最应该关注的主题。

turns.en: What I think actually is the most important theme here is around the way that the global economy is rewiring to focus more on resilience, and that's happening as a result of geopolitical competition, fragmentation, and a series of shocks. What's the portfolio implication? I would say there's a couple of things to consider.
turns.zh: 我认为这里真正最重要的主题，是全球经济正在重新布线（rewiring），把更多重心放在韧性（resilience）上，而这背后的推手是地缘政治竞争、碎片化和一连串冲击。这对投资组合意味着什么？我会说有几件事需要考虑。

turns.en: How do you want to get exposure to that resilience economy across the three pillars, whether it's AI, defense, or energy, and then the second critical point to tie it back to markets is how does that resilience economy fare in different macroeconomic regimes? Welcome to the bin, where we break down what's happening in the markets
turns.zh: 你想如何在这三大支柱上获得对韧性经济（resilience economy）的敞口——无论是人工智能、国防还是能源；而第二个把它和市场挂钩的关键问题是，这个韧性经济在不同的宏观经济环境下表现会如何？欢迎收听 The Bid，在这里我们拆解市场上正在发生的事，

turns.en: and explore the forces changing the economy and finance. I'm Oscar Polito. Today I'm joined by Anna Parker, part of the geopolitical research and strategy team at BlackRock and Yasmin Meisner, portfolio manager for thematic strategies of BlackRock.
turns.zh: 并探讨那些正在改变经济和金融的力量。我是 Oscar Pulido。今天做客节目的是 BlackRock 地缘政治研究与策略团队的 Anna Parker，以及 BlackRock 主题策略投资组合经理 Yasmin Meissner。

turns.en: Together we'll look beyond the geopolitical headlines and explore how a greater focus on national security and resilience is reshaping defense, energy, and technology. We'll discuss what these shifts could mean for markets, what the defense landscape is evolving, and the strategic vulnerabilities and choke points
turns.zh: 我们将一起跳出地缘政治的新闻头条，探讨对国家安全与韧性的更多重视正在如何重塑国防、能源和科技。我们会讨论这些转变对市场可能意味着什么、国防格局正在如何演变，以及那些战略脆弱点和咽喉节点（choke point），

turns.en: investors should be watching.
turns.zh: 这些正是投资者应当密切关注的地方。

turns.en: Anna and Yasmin, thank you so much for joining us on the bid. Thank you so much for having us Oscar. It's amazing to be here. Thanks for having us looking forward to a good discussion. Well, it's great to have you both on. We're going to talk about geopolitics and it's worth remembering that the BlackRock Investment Institute
turns.zh: Anna、Yasmin，非常感谢你们做客 The Bid。非常感谢你邀请我们，Oscar，能来到这里真是太棒了。谢谢邀请，期待有一场精彩的讨论。好的，非常高兴你们两位能来。我们要聊的是地缘政治，而值得记住的是，BlackRock Investment Institute

turns.en: a couple of years ago talked about a number of different mega forces. One of those was geopolitical fragmentation and a mega force really is meant to describe a structural theme that we think is going to be present in markets for many years to come.
turns.zh: 在几年前谈到过若干不同的宏观力量（mega forces），其中之一就是地缘政治碎片化（geopolitical fragmentation）。所谓宏观力量，其实是要描述一个我们认为会在未来很多年里持续存在于市场中的结构性主题。

turns.en: So it's fair to say that there's a lot of noise going on right now with respect to geopolitics and Anna, if I could start with you, when you step back from the headlines, what's the bigger story that investors should focus on? I think you're right that the headlines tend to focus on volatility, shock, churn, chaos, and the environment.
turns.zh: 所以可以说，眼下地缘政治方面有非常多的噪音。Anna，我可以先从你开始吗——当你跳出新闻头条往后退一步看，投资者应该关注的更大的故事是什么？我觉得你说得对，头条往往聚焦于波动、冲击、翻搅，以及环境中的混乱。

turns.en: But that's really not the most important theme for investors to focus on, and certainly not for long-term investors. What I think actually is the most important theme here is around the way that the global economy is rewiring to focus more on resilience, and that's happening as a result of geopolitical competition,
turns.zh: 但那真的不是投资者最该关注的主题，对长期投资者来说尤其如此。我认为这里真正最重要的主题，是全球经济正在重新布线，把更多重心放在韧性上，而这一变化的推手是地缘政治竞争、

turns.en: fragmentation, and a series of shocks. So if you break down what's happening, the first thing is that competition between the US and China is accelerating and intensifying, and that's particularly true around AI. We see this as a structural and durable fact about the world,
turns.zh: 碎片化以及一连串冲击。所以如果把正在发生的事情拆开来看，第一件事是美国与中国之间的竞争正在加速和加剧，在人工智能领域尤其如此。我们把这看作关于这个世界的一个结构性、且会长期存在的事实，

turns.en: and one that extends well beyond this period of stability in the US-China relationship that we're in right now. The second thing I would say is about fragmentation. You mentioned that BlackRock's Investment Institute sees geopolitical fragmentation as an important theme shaping the global economy.
turns.zh: 而且它远远超出了我们当前所处的这段中美关系稳定期。我想说的第二件事是关于碎片化。你提到 BlackRock Investment Institute 把地缘政治碎片化视为塑造全球经济的一个重要主题。

turns.en: That remains true. When we coined that term, we did so to talk about the world organizing itself as a result of US-China competition into different blocks. And what we're seeing right now is actually yet another round of fragmentation that's happening as a result of the US moving to reset its relationships geopolitically and economically
turns.zh: 这一点依然成立。当初我们创造这个词，是为了描述世界因为中美竞争而自行组织成不同的集团（blocs）。而我们现在看到的，其实是又一轮碎片化，其成因是美国开始在地缘政治和经济上重置它

turns.en: with the rest of the world. The other thing is the Iran War. This is the latest in a series of shocks, fundamentally disruptive to the global economy, and it's the latest on top of a variety of other shocks that we've seen over the last five years, record inflation, trade disruption, the COVID pandemic, Russia's invasion of Ukraine.
turns.zh: 与世界其他地区的关系。另一件事是伊朗战争。这是一系列冲击中的最新一个，对全球经济有根本性的破坏力；而在它之前，过去五年我们已经见识过各种其他冲击：创纪录的通胀、贸易中断、新冠疫情、俄罗斯入侵乌克兰。

turns.en: So competition, fragmentation, shocks, they're all coming together to do a few things for us. First is exposing the vulnerabilities and the global economy that stem from dependency, and the ways that those dependencies can become weaponized in times of geopolitical conflict or stress. We've seen two examples of that in the last two years.
turns.zh: 所以竞争、碎片化、冲击，它们合在一起为我们做了几件事。第一，暴露出全球经济中源于依赖的脆弱性，以及这些依赖在地缘政治冲突或压力时期如何被武器化（weaponized）。过去两年我们已经看到两个这样的例子。

turns.en: The first was the emergence of a choke point in the technology supply chain around critical minerals and rare earths. And the second is a physical choke point in the global energy market at the straight of horror moves during the Iran War.
turns.zh: 第一个是技术供应链上围绕关键矿产（critical minerals）和稀土（rare earths）出现的咽喉节点。第二个则是伊朗战争期间，全球能源市场上一个实体层面的咽喉节点——霍尔木兹海峡（Strait of Hormuz）。

turns.en: What countries are doing in response to this is thinking about what are their dependencies that they can de-risk and what are those that are not going to be tolerable over time. We're seeing major investments to reduce dependencies in strategic sectors, certainly energy, defense, technology. This is the global resilience economy.
turns.zh: 各国对此的应对，是思考自己有哪些依赖可以去风险化（de-risk），又有哪些依赖随着时间推移将变得无法容忍。我们看到在战略行业出现了大规模投资来降低依赖，尤其是能源、国防、科技。这就是全球韧性经济。

turns.en: On energy, we see a huge amount of investment going towards energy security. On defense, global defense spending increased significantly for the last 11 years in a row. We're up about 40% just over the last decade on technology. Obviously, this is the largest capex cycle that we've seen in history.
turns.zh: 在能源方面，我们看到有巨量投资流向能源安全。在国防方面，全球国防开支已经连续 11 年显著增长，仅过去十年就上升了约 40%。在科技方面，显然，这是我们历史上所见规模最大的一轮资本开支周期（capex cycle）。

turns.en: A lot of that is animated and shaped by competition between the US and China, but also the desire for countries in between them to pursue technology sovereignty. When we talk about geopolitics, I think we often think about the latest conflict that's in the headlines and the short-term impact on markets.
turns.zh: 其中很大一部分是由美中之间的竞争所驱动和塑造的，同时也源于夹在两国之间的其他国家追求技术主权（technology sovereignty）的愿望。谈到地缘政治时，我想我们往往会想到头条上最新的那场冲突，以及它对市场的短期影响。

turns.en: And Anna, what you've helped us do is zoom out and really think about this more strategically. This is a lot to unpack here. And Yasmin, maybe I could come to you. If you're an investor, what does all of this mean for markets? And how are you seeing it from your seat?
turns.zh: 而 Anna，你帮我们做的是把镜头拉远，真正从更战略的角度去思考这件事。这里要展开的内容很多。Yasmin，也许我可以把话题转到你这边。如果你是一名投资者，这一切对市场意味着什么？从你的位置上你是怎么看的？

turns.en: Anna, introduce this idea of the resilience economy across three core pillars that's energy, defense, and AI. The three are linked to each other. AI needs power, any country that's thinking seriously about its defense strategy is going to care an awful lot about its energy security.
turns.zh: Anna 提出了韧性经济这个概念，它有三大核心支柱，也就是能源、国防和人工智能。这三者彼此关联。人工智能需要电力；任何一个认真思考自身国防战略的国家，都会极其在意自己的能源安全。

turns.en: Defense increasingly is being characterized by technology, so think of autonomous weapons. And then AI, as Anna said, is becoming a strategic asset for countries. And so is something that needs to be defended and is becoming a focal part of the US-China competition.
turns.zh: 国防正越来越多地由技术来定义，可以想想自主武器（autonomous weapons）。而人工智能，正如 Anna 所说，正在成为各国的一项战略资产，因此它是需要被守护的东西，也正在成为中美竞争的一个焦点部分。

turns.en: Now, what's interesting about the three, alongside them being linked, we're also seeing them increasingly compete for capital. So Anna talked about the ways in which some of the big US hyperscaler companies are investing huge amounts in AI. The latest estimate I've seen is in excess of $1.3 trillion next year. Why is that significant?
turns.zh: 现在，这三者之间有意思的地方在于，除了彼此关联，我们还看到它们在越来越多地争夺资本。Anna 谈到美国一些大型超大规模云计算公司（hyperscalers）正在人工智能上投入巨额资金。我看到的最新估计是，明年将超过 1.3 万亿美元。为什么这一点很重要？

turns.en: Well, previously, a lot of these companies funded those investments through their own cash flows. Now we are seeing a growing share of them move into credit markets to help fund that incremental capital need. We have governments increasing their commitments to defense.
turns.zh: 因为此前，这些公司中的很多是用自身现金流来为这些投资融资的。而现在我们看到，越来越多的公司开始转向信用债市场，来帮助满足这部分增量资本需求。同时各国政府也在提高对国防的投入承诺。

turns.en: So we saw NATO allies committing around 5% of their GDP to defense spend by 2035. When you think about what's the portfolio implication, I would say there's a couple of things to consider. So the first is, how do you want to get exposure to that resilience economy across the three pillars, whether it's AI defense or energy?
turns.zh: 我们看到 NATO 盟国承诺到 2035 年将约 5% 的 GDP 用于国防开支。当你思考这对投资组合意味着什么时，我会说有几件事需要考虑。第一件是，你想如何在这三大支柱上获得对韧性经济的敞口——无论是人工智能、国防还是能源？

turns.en: Do you want to have that exposure in equities, in credit or in private markets or across all three? And then the second critical point to tie it back to markets is how does that resilience economy fare in different macroeconomic regimes?
turns.zh: 你想通过股票、信用债还是私募市场来持有这种敞口，或者三者都要？第二件把话题拉回市场的关键要点是，这个韧性经济在不同的宏观经济环境（macroeconomic regimes）下表现如何？

turns.en: So in a world where inflation may be stickier for longer or rates may be higher, how do those different aspects of the resilience economy fare in that world? And what elements of them do you want to lean into in your portfolios? And Anna, maybe then we can dig in a little bit on some of these sectors.
turns.zh: 也就是说，在一个通胀可能更黏着、持续更久，或者利率可能更高的世界里，韧性经济的这些不同侧面在那个世界里表现如何？你又希望在投资组合里加码其中的哪些部分？那么 Anna，接下来也许我们可以就其中一些行业深入聊一聊。

turns.en: Let's start with energy because certainly the Iran war has exposed how quickly geopolitics can reverberate through energy markets. Anybody who's putting fuel in a vehicle will have noticed the increase in gas prices. So what have we learned about the global energy system and where it's headed as a result of this conflict?
turns.zh: 我们先从能源开始，因为伊朗战争无疑已经暴露出地缘政治能多么迅速地在能源市场引起连锁反应。任何给车加过油的人都会注意到汽油价格的上涨。那么，透过这场冲突，我们对全球能源体系以及它将走向何方，学到了什么？

turns.en: Maybe I'll take your question in two parts. So the first about what we've learned so far. And I think it's been remarkable to see how resilient the global energy market has actually been amidst record disruption.
turns.zh: 也许我把你的问题分成两部分来回答。第一部分关于我们目前学到了什么。我觉得非常了不起的一点是，在创纪录的中断之中，全球能源市场实际上表现得如此有韧性。

turns.en: When the Iran war first broke out, we saw a near immediate displacement of about 20% of the world oil supply and 20% of global LNG exports. This led to well reason concerns that oil could move up to 150, 200 dollars of barrel and these concerns proved wrong.
turns.zh: 伊朗战争刚爆发时，我们看到全球约 20% 的石油供应和 20% 的液化天然气（LNG）出口几乎立刻被切断。这引发了相当有理由的担忧，认为油价可能涨到每桶 150 甚至 200 美元——而这些担忧最终被证明是错的。

turns.en: So why is that we saw a series of stabilizers come together in a somewhat unexpected way. There are three stories to this. The first is in the Middle East where pipelines that were purpose built for exactly this type of moment by Saudi Arabia and the UAE created an immediate bypass to the straight of hormones when it became weaponized.
turns.zh: 那为什么会这样？因为我们看到一系列稳定器以某种出人意料的方式汇聚到了一起。这里面有三个故事。第一个发生在中东：沙特阿拉伯和阿联酋当初正是为这种时刻专门修建的管道，在霍尔木兹海峡被武器化时，立刻形成了一条绕行通道。

turns.en: As a result of that bypass combined with the use of ship to ship transfers in the Persian Gulf. We've seen just in recent weeks the share of Middle Eastern oil exports resume at about 98% of the pre war level. I would say that this is vulnerable. This is a point in time, but it's a pretty remarkable story around resilience.
turns.zh: 由于这条绕行通道，再加上在波斯湾使用船对船（ship-to-ship）转运，就在最近几周，我们看到中东石油出口已经恢复到战前水平的约 98%。我会说这仍然是脆弱的，这只是某一个时点的状况，但它确实是一个相当了不起的关于韧性的故事。

turns.en: The second story is a global one after the conflict started the International Energy Administration organized and coordinated a historic drawdown. Of strategic stockpiles. This was the largest coordinated release in history.
turns.zh: 第二个故事是全球层面的。冲突爆发后，国际能源署（International Energy Agency，IEA）组织并协调了一次历史性的战略储备（strategic stockpiles）释放。这是历史上规模最大的一次协同释放。

turns.en: And as part of that, the United States pulled down its strategic petroleum reserve, which enabled it to release additional barrels of oil into the global market. When the conflict began, the global market was already quite well supplied. So the global liquidity and resilient story as well.
turns.zh: 作为其中的一部分，美国动用了自己的战略石油储备（strategic petroleum reserve），从而得以向全球市场额外释放一批原油。冲突开始时，全球市场本来供应就已经相当充足。所以这也是一个关于全球流动性和韧性的故事。

turns.en: The third story is I think the most unexpected and that is what China did to stabilize the market. We saw China significantly draw back its oil imports during the conflict from the time the conflict began to about June. That was a 50% reduction in oil imports for a major oil consumer.
turns.zh: 第三个故事我认为是我最没料到的，那就是中国为稳定市场所做的事。我们看到在冲突期间中国大幅削减了石油进口——从冲突开始到大约 6 月，作为一个主要石油消费国，中国的石油进口减少了 50%。

turns.en: I think there are debates about whether this was a strategic decision by China or one that is more circumstantial. But the result is that China had significant energy reserves going into the conflict. And they primed their domestic economy through a switch over to electrification and a push towards electrification over the last decades.
turns.zh: 我想对于这究竟是中国的战略性决策，还是更多出于形势所迫，是存在争论的。但结果是，中国在进入这场冲突时拥有可观的能源储备。而且过去几十年，他们通过向电气化（electrification）的切换和持续推进，为国内经济提前做好了准备。

turns.en: This was a surprise to a lot of observers, including energy experts. I would offer a couple of caveats though. The first being that some of these buffers that had existed in the system and prevented a worst case scenario are beginning to draw down.
turns.zh: 这让很多观察人士感到意外，包括能源专家。不过我要提出几点保留意见。第一，系统中原本存在、并阻止了最坏情形出现的一些缓冲，正在开始被消耗。

turns.en: The second thing is we see the renewed risk of conflict escalation, putting some of those bypass routes in jeopardy. And we've certainly seen resilience in the crude market, not translate evenly to the refined product markets, which is why we see gasoline prices, diesel and jet fuel under historic strain.
turns.zh: 第二，我们看到冲突升级的风险重新出现，使其中一些绕行通道面临危险。而且我们确实看到，原油市场上的韧性并没有均匀地传导到成品油市场——这就是为什么我们看到汽油、柴油和航空燃油价格正承受历史性的压力。

turns.en: Right. So what you're saying is that even with the disruption in the Middle East, what many people might not realize is maybe how much worse it could have been. Correct. Energy security is this big piece of the resilience economy story.
turns.zh: 明白。所以你的意思是，即便中东出现了这样的中断，很多人可能没有意识到的是，情况原本可能会糟糕得多。没错。能源安全是韧性经济这个故事中非常重要的一块。

turns.en: So if you look back at history, all of these buffers in the system were created in response to prior crises and shocks. The 1970s in the Arab oil embargo and the shocks that resulted from that, those shocks brought us the creation of the International Energy Administration and more international coordination.
turns.zh: 如果回望历史，系统中的所有这些缓冲，都是为了应对先前的危机和冲击而建立的。1970 年代的阿拉伯石油禁运以及由此产生的冲击，那些冲击促成了国际能源署的创立，也带来了更多的国际协调。

turns.en: They brought the creation of strategic reserves and that coordination function that comes withdrawing those down. And then even beyond the Middle East, war in Ukraine prompted the Europeans to think a lot more about diversifying their energy markets as a result of being cut off from Russian gas.
turns.zh: 它们还促成了战略储备的建立，以及在动用这些储备时所需的协调职能。而即使把视野放到中东之外，乌克兰战争也促使欧洲人去更多地思考如何让能源市场多元化，因为他们被切断了俄罗斯天然气供应。

turns.en: And I think the question is what investments we're going to see right now that are going to be made to create yet more resilience to future shocks. I think this could look like a few things, certainly diversification of routes.
turns.zh: 我认为问题在于，我们现在会看到哪些投资，被用来为未来的冲击创造更多韧性。我觉得这可能表现为几件事，首先是运输路线的多元化。

turns.en: We're already seeing major investments announced around pipeline facilities in the Middle East and connecting those closer to key markets. We're seeing expansion of building out storage capacity that's closer to customers downstream. And I also think we're going to see a major conversation about diversification of energy sources.
turns.zh: 我们已经看到中东宣布了一批围绕管道设施的重大投资，把这些设施连接到更靠近关键市场的位置。我们看到储存能力在扩容，建设的储备设施更贴近下游客户。我还认为，我们将看到一场关于能源来源多元化的重要讨论。

turns.en: This is mostly about optionality, much more so than energy independence writ large. And this is even more important amidst the kind of historic demands on power that we're seeing as a result of the AI infrastructure build out.
turns.zh: 这主要关乎可选择性（optionality），而不是宽泛意义上的能源独立。而在我们看到因人工智能基础设施建设而带来的那种历史级电力需求之下，这一点就更加重要了。

turns.en: Yes, but maybe I could come back to you because you also mentioned the defense sector as one of the themes here that we need to be paying attention to. And your team recently returned from a space and defense tour, meaning that you were meeting with companies. What were some of the takeaways from that tour?
turns.zh: 是的。不过也许我可以把话题转到你这边，因为你也提到国防行业是这里我们需要关注的主题之一。你的团队最近刚结束一趟太空与国防的调研行程，也就是说你们去会见了一些公司。那趟行程有哪些收获？

turns.en: So Anna talked a little bit about the Iran conflict and the implications of that from an energy perspective. There was a CBO study that came out recently, which said up to two thirds of the US Patriot interceptors have now been used during the course of this conflict.
turns.zh: Anna 刚才谈了一些伊朗冲突，以及从能源角度看它的影响。最近有一份 CBO 的研究报告指出，在这场冲突过程中，美国的 Patriot 拦截弹（Patriot interceptors）已经用掉了最多三分之二。

turns.en: So as a reminder, these interceptors are used to defend against the likes of drones or missiles. The drones in question are very cheap to produce, so in the region of 50k, but the Patriot interceptors are pretty expensive to produce in the range of $5 million and have very long lead times in some cases more than two years.
turns.zh: 提醒一下，这些拦截弹是用来防御无人机或导弹一类目标的。而这里说的无人机生产成本非常低，大约在 5 万美元这个量级；但 Patriot 拦截弹的生产相当昂贵，大约在 500 万美元这个区间，而且交付周期非常长，某些情况下超过两年。

turns.en: And so that already tees us up for a particular challenge that the military is facing in terms of how do you commit that capital? How do you replenish those stockpiles that we've seen get drawn down over the last few months? There are a number of companies that are really focused on solving some of these problems.
turns.zh: 所以这已经为军方摆出了一个特定的挑战：你要如何投入这笔资本？你要如何补充那些我们在过去几个月里看到被消耗掉的库存？有很多公司正真正专注于解决其中一些问题。

turns.en: And I would say that our team came back incredibly energized and excited about the pace of innovation that they saw. It talked about the challenges around drone technology. You're trying to defend against low cost high volume drones. One of the companies that they met produces counter drone technology by using microwave fields.
turns.zh: 我会说，我们团队回来时精神极其振奋，对他们所看到的创新速度感到兴奋。前面谈到了无人机技术方面的挑战：你要防御的是低成本、大批量的无人机。他们会见的其中一家公司，用微波场来做反无人机（counter-drone）技术。

turns.en: So the idea is you create an interference field, you can protect against a drone swarm. It's a completely different way of thinking about defending against drones as an example. A lot of these companies are very focused on making their manufacturing simple and scalable.
turns.zh: 举这个例子是想说，这是一种完全不同的思考如何防御无人机的方式：你制造一个干扰场，就能防御无人机蜂群（drone swarm）。这些公司当中有很多都非常专注于让自己的制造变得简单且可规模化。

turns.en: In some cases, they're even bringing their full supply chain in house so that they have total end-to-end control. It matters because as technology evolves incredibly quickly, we need to have supply chains that are flexible, robust, to sustain munitions through time in any kind of conflict.
turns.zh: 在某些情况下，他们甚至把整条供应链都收归内部，以便对端到端拥有完全的掌控。这一点之所以重要，是因为技术演进极快，我们需要拥有灵活、稳健的供应链，才能在任何类型的冲突中长期维持弹药供给。

turns.en: Ukraine is really good at this. Ukraine can produce up to 8 million drones annually. They also have a six-week learning cycle within their kind of battlefield. So in other words, they adapt very quickly as the technology changes. The third point is around space. Space is another frontier for defense.
turns.zh: 乌克兰在这方面做得非常出色。乌克兰每年最多能生产 800 万架无人机。他们在自己的战场上还有一个六周的学习周期。换句话说，随着技术变化，他们适应得非常快。第三点是关于太空。太空是国防的另一个前沿。

turns.en: SpaceX has had a very important role to play here. It's just brought launch costs down. Why does that matter for the US military? Well, it basically means they can put stuff up in space a lot more cheaply and a lot more easily. Satellite data as an example, you can use to identify targets, the team at a company called K2 Space,
turns.zh: SpaceX 在这里扮演了非常重要的角色，它就是把发射成本降了下来。这对美军为什么重要？基本上这意味着他们能以低得多、也容易得多的方式把东西送上太空。举个例子，卫星数据可以用来识别目标；有一家叫 K2 Space 的公司，其团队

turns.en: that company puts really large load satellites up in space. So a normal satellite has about two kilowatts of power. That's the equivalent of a kettle. This company is able to put up 20 kilowatts, so significantly bigger. The reason why I mention it, when they get this big, it becomes much harder for adversaries to then jam the data.
turns.zh: 会把载荷非常大的卫星送上太空。一颗普通卫星大约有 2 千瓦的功率，这相当于一个电水壶。而这家公司能够送上 20 千瓦，所以要大得多。我之所以提到这一点，是因为当卫星大到这种程度时，对手要干扰其数据就会困难得多。

turns.en: So it allows the military to have reliable and consistent data from space using these really large satellites that gives the US military that edge. The other big takeaway is that the space use cases are extending way beyond satellites. We're talking about putting interceptors in space or putting in different types of arsenal in space.
turns.zh: 所以这让军方能够借助这些非常大的卫星，从太空获得可靠且持续的数据，从而赋予美军那种优势。另一个大的收获是，太空的应用场景正在远远超出卫星本身。我们说的是把拦截弹部署到太空，或者在太空部署不同类型的武器库。

turns.en: It's a really exciting and innovative area. We're looking at different use cases of technology, establishing that supply chain and ensuring that we have that large capacity to really be able to maintain a conflict through time.
turns.zh: 这是一个非常令人兴奋、也非常有创新性的领域。我们在看技术的不同应用场景，建立那条供应链，并确保我们拥有那种大规模产能，从而真正能够把一场冲突长期维持下去。

turns.en: We did talk to Reid Mengi recently about the space economy, and so you're touching on how space is becoming even more relevant to the conversation. Yasmin, the pace of change in this space, no pun intended, is remarkable.
turns.zh: 我们最近确实和 Reid Menge 聊过太空经济，所以你正好触及了太空在这个话题中变得多么重要。Yasmin，这个 space 领域的变化速度实在惊人——我可没有故意拿“太空”玩双关。

turns.en: And you mentioned the Ukrainian government as an example of a government that seems to be able to adapt pretty quickly. How are governments keeping up with the pace of change in the defense sector? Yes, I think the US military is a really fascinating example of this.
turns.zh: 你还提到乌克兰政府，作为一个似乎能够相当快速适应的政府的例子。各国政府是如何跟上国防领域变化速度的？是的，我觉得美军在这方面是一个非常引人入胜的例子。

turns.en: If you think back to how the military was architected before, we lived in a world that was much more driven by hardware. So you imagine you had a plane, the plane had its own software and its own command control system in it.
turns.zh: 如果你回想军队以前是如何架构的，我们生活在一个更多由硬件驱动的世界里。你可以想象，你有一架飞机，这架飞机里面有自己的软件和自己的指挥控制系统（command and control system）。

turns.en: Then you had a drone with its own command and control system in it, and then maybe you had a tank and same thing again. So all of those three things separate and don't necessarily speak the same language or talk to each other.
turns.zh: 然后你有一架无人机，里面也有自己的指挥控制系统；接着也许你还有一辆坦克，情况又是一样。所以这三样东西彼此分离，未必说同一种语言，也未必能相互对话。

turns.en: The military is increasingly trying to move towards creating this software that becomes this sort of architecture of their whole military system. So in other words, you have a single command and control system that speaks the same language and you slot your hardware modules into it. And that obviously creates a much greater efficiency.
turns.zh: 军方正越来越多地试图走向创造这样一套软件，让它成为整个军事系统的架构。换句话说，你有一套单一的指挥控制系统，说着同一种语言，然后你把硬件模块插进去。这显然带来了大得多的效率。

turns.en: It means that the software becomes the brain and the hardware becomes the different body parts. And it allows you to make decisions much more quickly because you can take information from all these different places, put it together and basically decide on a list of targets
turns.zh: 这意味着软件成为大脑，硬件成为不同的身体部位。它让你能够快得多地做出决策，因为你可以把来自所有这些不同地方的信息汇集到一起，基本上列出一份目标清单，

turns.en: and which one is the most optimal target and move very quickly to execute on that. Right, it sounds like the suppliers to governments is broadening out. There's more companies making more goods for governments to consume to help with their defense budgets. And you mentioned technology and AI. So it's a good segue, Anna, back to you.
turns.zh: 并判断哪一个是最优目标，然后非常迅速地去执行。明白，听起来政府的供应商群体正在扩大。有更多公司在为政府生产更多产品，来支撑它们的国防预算。你还提到了科技和人工智能。所以这是个很好的过渡，Anna，把话题交回给你。

turns.en: You mentioned energy, defense, and technology as three themes here. So let's talk about technology and tell me about how you see geopolitics shaping the AI growth story. You talked earlier about the US, China, dynamic being very central to the geopolitical story.
turns.zh: 你提到能源、国防和科技是这里的三大主题。那我们就来聊聊科技，跟我说说你认为地缘政治正在如何塑造人工智能的增长故事。你之前谈到美中之间的动态是地缘政治故事的核心。

turns.en: So what does technology sovereignty actually mean for geopolitics and for investors? I think again, take this in two parts. The first is about the US and China. So this is really at the center of the AI growth story and the global AI infrastructure buildout.
turns.zh: 那么，技术主权对地缘政治和投资者来说究竟意味着什么？我想还是分两部分来讲。第一部分关于美国和中国。这确实处在人工智能增长故事和全球人工智能基础设施建设（AI infrastructure buildout）的中心。

turns.en: Both the US and China believe that AI is going to deliver the defining military and economic advantage of the century, in part for some of the reasons that Yasmin just talked about. The headline when you think about US China AI competition tends to focus on benchmark model performance, who's ahead and who's behind.
turns.zh: 美中两国都相信，人工智能将带来本世纪最具决定性的军事和经济优势，部分原因正是 Yasmin 刚才谈到的那些。而当你想到美中人工智能竞争时，头条往往聚焦于模型的基准测试表现——谁领先、谁落后。

turns.en: But I think that this technology competition really runs the gamut of the full stack, including the race to secure the inputs needed in order to dominate and have a reliance within that technology stack.
turns.zh: 但我认为，这场技术竞争实际上贯穿了整个技术栈（full stack）的全部环节，其中也包括一场竞赛：确保拿到所需的各项投入品，从而在这一技术栈中占据主导地位并具备韧性。

turns.en: The US and China are both taking steps to protect their own technology stacks and to shore up their advantages and to ensure that no one can infringe upon their advantages. But we see the ways in which the AI supply chain is still really globalized.
turns.zh: 美中两国都在采取措施保护自己的技术栈、巩固自身优势，并确保没有人能够侵犯它们的优势。但我们也看到，人工智能供应链在多大程度上仍然是真正全球化的。

turns.en: AI related hardware shipments last year rose by 40% and this accounted for a third of global trade growth. McKinsey gives a good example of a data center in the US that is running US frontier models using US design chips. But those chips were made in Taiwan using equipment from the Netherlands.
turns.zh: 去年与人工智能相关的硬件出货量增长了 40%，这占了全球贸易增长的三分之一。McKinsey 举了一个很好的例子：美国的一座数据中心，运行着美国的前沿模型（frontier models），用的是美国设计的芯片。但这些芯片是在台湾用来自荷兰的设备制造的。

turns.en: They are paired with high bandwidth memory chips that were made in Korea, packaged and tested in Southeast Asia. Maybe they're being powered by turbines from Mexico and wired with copper from Chile. So we see the kind of globalized nature of the AI supply chain here.
turns.zh: 这些芯片还配上了在韩国制造、在东南亚封装和测试的高带宽内存（HBM，high-bandwidth memory）芯片。也许它们的电力来自墨西哥生产的涡轮机，布线用的是来自智利的铜。所以我们在这里看到了人工智能供应链的那种全球化性质。

turns.en: So no country right now is capable of fully building that stack on their own. But even the US and China with the most advanced AI ecosystems have significant dependencies that sit outside their borders.
turns.zh: 所以目前没有任何一个国家能够完全靠自己去构建那一整套技术栈。但即便是拥有人工智能生态系统最先进的美国和中国，也存在大量位于其国境之外的依赖。

turns.en: So I think the real question is whether that interdependence stabilizes the global technology build out or whether it destabilizes this major economic bet that the world is making around AI.
turns.zh: 所以我认为真正的问题是，这种相互依赖究竟会稳定全球的技术建设，还是会动摇世界围绕人工智能所做的这个重大经济押注。

turns.en: I do want to think a little bit more about what's happening in the rest of the world outside of the US and China because that's not the only story here. Rather than joining the race to self-reliance, other countries are thinking about how to ensure the sovereignty and the security of their own technology supply chains.
turns.zh: 我确实想再多谈一谈美国和中国的国境之外、世界其他地区正在发生什么，因为那并不是这里唯一的故事。其他国家并不是加入这场自力更生的竞赛，而是在思考如何确保自身技术供应链的主权和安全。

turns.en: So you asked about what technology sovereignty actually looks like. To me, this is really about managed interdependence. If you think about AI as critical infrastructure, which it increasingly is, if you're a country, you have to ensure that your critical infrastructure is impervious to threats that it's reliable in the time of crisis.
turns.zh: 你问到技术主权实际上是什么样子。在我看来，这真正关乎的是有管理的相互依赖（managed interdependence）。如果你把人工智能看作关键基础设施——它正越来越是这样——那么作为一个国家，你必须确保自己的关键基础设施不受威胁影响，在危机时刻是可靠的。

turns.en: A country can decide that either they want to or they have to rely on foreign technology for models or for chips, but they care a lot about whether
turns.zh: 一个国家可以决定，它要么愿意、要么不得不依赖外国的模型技术或芯片技术，但它非常在意的是：

turns.en: compute sits within their own borders, whether sensitive data is allowed to leave the country, and whether they have reliable and guaranteed access to the inputs that they need in the event of crisis. So what we see is a layer by layer resilience play that's happening.
turns.zh: 算力（compute）是否位于自己的国境之内，敏感数据是否被允许出境，以及在危机发生时，它能否可靠且有保证地获得自己所需的那些投入品。所以我们看到的，是一场逐层展开的韧性布局。

turns.en: So countries at the input layer are thinking about and doubling down on areas where they have advantages, whether that's critical minerals, whether that's energy or perhaps memory chips as examples of those other choke point advantages in that globalized supply chain.
turns.zh: 在投入品这一层，各国正在思考并加码自己有优势的领域，无论是关键矿产、能源，还是可能是内存芯片——这些都是那条全球化供应链上其他一些咽喉节点优势的例子。

turns.en: At the model layer, countries are increasingly cultivating their own national champion AI labs. We see this with cohere in Canada, Mistral and France, G 42 and the UAE and the like. At the compute layer, a major expansion of data centers is happening outside the US and China.
turns.zh: 在模型这一层，各国正越来越多地培育自己的国家级冠军人工智能实验室。我们在加拿大的 Cohere、法国的 Mistral、阿联酋的 G42 等公司身上看到了这一点。在算力这一层，一场大规模的数据中心扩张正在美国和中国之外发生。

turns.en: We see super fast growth in data center markets in Southeast Asia with Malaysia projected to quadruple its data center construction just in the next two years. These are examples of the ways in which we see a really dynamic conversation and evolving around AI technology sovereignty globally.
turns.zh: 我们看到东南亚的数据中心市场增长极快，其中马来西亚预计仅在未来两年内数据中心建设规模就会翻两番。这些都是例子，说明我们看到围绕人工智能技术主权，全球正在进行一场非常活跃、且不断演变的讨论。

turns.en: And I like that term that you used managed interdependence, which sounds like countries don't have access to all parts of the stack or all of the inputs that go into having the technological sovereignty. But when talking to Anna, she used the word choke point.
turns.zh: 我很喜欢你用的那个词——有管理的相互依赖。听起来是说，各国并不能拿到技术栈的所有环节，也无法获得实现技术主权所需的全部投入品。但在和 Anna 交流时，她用到了“咽喉节点”这个词。

turns.en: And so what is that next strategic choke point that we should be paying attention to? It's interesting. We talked about the resilience economy. We talked about these three pillars across AI defense and energy. And I think it's worth me aware of exactly that question, Oscar.
turns.zh: 那么，下一个我们应该关注的战略咽喉节点是什么？有意思的是，我们谈了韧性经济，谈了人工智能、国防和能源这三大支柱。我觉得正好值得我来回答这个问题，Oscar。

turns.en: What are those choke points and what's the implication for investors? So one example would be rare earths China mines around 60% of the world's rare earths and refines little more than 90% of the world's rare earths. Rare earths go into magnets magnets in turn have a range of important uses from a defense perspective.
turns.zh: 那些咽喉节点是什么，对投资者又有什么影响？一个例子是稀土：中国开采了全球约 60% 的稀土，并精炼了略高于 90% 的全球稀土。稀土被用于制造磁体，而磁体从国防角度看有一系列重要用途。

turns.en: They matter because they go into fighter jets from an AI perspective. As Anna said, they matter because they go into say data centers. So they are strategically important. And what you have seen are countries like the US trying to partner with the likes of Australia and Japan to move away from relying as much on China
turns.zh: 它们之所以重要，是因为它们被用在战斗机上；而从人工智能角度看，正如 Anna 所说，它们之所以重要，是因为它们被用在比如数据中心里。所以它们具有战略重要性。而你已经看到的是，像美国这样的国家正试图与澳大利亚、日本等国家合作，以减少对中国的依赖，

turns.en: by building out their own domestic supply chain, both from a mining and refining perspective. What's really interesting is you see, for example, the US even being willing to set a price floor that's more than double the market price to really try to encourage domestic producers to start mining in this space.
turns.zh: 方式是从开采和精炼两个环节都建起自己的国内供应链。真正有意思的是，比如你会看到美国甚至愿意设定一个高于市场价格两倍以上的价格下限（price floor），以真正鼓励国内生产商开始在这一领域开采。

turns.en: So that's a kind of area of strategic weakness for the rest of the world and an area of strength for China. On semiconductors, the reality is Taiwan produces more than 90% of the world's semiconductors and sits in a geopolitical hotspot.
turns.zh: 所以这对世界其他地区来说是某种战略弱点，对中国来说则是一个优势领域。在半导体（semiconductors）方面，现实是台湾生产了全球 90% 以上的半导体，而且身处一个地缘政治热点地区。

turns.en: When we move towards a world that's increasingly characterized by autonomous weapons and AI, clearly having access to advanced computational power and being able to replenish stockpiles through time becomes incredibly important.
turns.zh: 当我们走向一个日益以自主武器和人工智能为特征的世界时，显然，能够获得先进算力、并且能够随时间不断补充库存，就变得极其重要。

turns.en: Clearly, China uses rare earth as a point of leverage, but you've also seen the US use semis as a point of leverage in their relationship with China. And then the last example I'd give on the energy side, countries increasingly attacking energy infrastructure as a way again to exploit their adversaries.
turns.zh: 显然，中国把稀土当作一个筹码（leverage），但你也看到美国在与中国的关系中把半导体当作筹码。最后我想举的一个例子是在能源方面：各国越来越多地攻击能源基础设施，以此作为又一次打击对手的手段。

turns.en: Ukraine, in the first eight months of 2026, the Russian refinery was attacked once every three days. So the point is that different countries identify these areas of strategic weakness and choose to exploit them.
turns.zh: 乌克兰方面，在 2026 年的头八个月里，俄罗斯的炼油厂平均每三天就遭到一次攻击。所以要点在于，不同国家会识别出这些战略弱点区域，并选择去加以利用。

turns.en: And so I certainly think each of those three are from an investment perspective, incredibly important to track, not only how the US-China relationship evolves,
turns.zh: 所以我当然认为，从投资角度看，这三者中的每一个都极其重要，需要跟踪的不仅是美中关系如何演变，

turns.en: but also how access to these supply chains evolved through time, because they certainly have the capability to really impact energy security, ability to operate AI, but also the future world of defense as well.
turns.zh: 还有对这些供应链的获取渠道如何随时间演变，因为它们确实有能力真正影响能源安全、影响运营人工智能的能力，也影响未来的国防世界。

turns.en: And I think back to where we started, Anna, we said, often times we look at the headlines, we think about the short-term impact on markets, volatility, and what should I be doing in my portfolio for the short term when these headlines hit?
turns.zh: 我想起我们开始的地方，Anna。我们说过，很多时候我们看着新闻头条，想的是对市场的短期影响、波动，以及当这些头条出现时，我在短期内应该对自己的投资组合做些什么？

turns.en: And really my reflection is that this probably has more strategic implications for investor portfolios in terms of how they're allocating what part of the world they're allocating and the sorts of risk that they're taking.
turns.zh: 而我真正的感想是，这件事对投资者组合的影响可能更具战略性——体现在他们如何进行配置、配置世界的哪些部分，以及他们承担哪一类风险。

turns.en: So thanks for helping us look beyond the short-term headlines and really understand the implications that geopolitics is having on things like energy, defense, technology. This seems like it's going to be a story that is going to continue to develop, so we look forward to having you back.
turns.zh: 所以感谢你们帮助我们跳出短期头条，真正理解地缘政治正在对能源、国防、科技等领域产生的影响。这看起来会是一个持续发展下去的故事，所以我们期待你们再次来做客。

turns.en: Thanks for sharing these insights and thanks for doing it here on the bit. Thanks so much, Oscar. Thanks for having us. Thanks for listening to this episode of The Bit.
turns.zh: 谢谢你们分享这些洞见，也谢谢你们选择在 The Bid 上分享。非常感谢，Oscar。谢谢邀请我们。感谢各位收听本期 The Bid。

turns.en: If you enjoyed this conversation, check out my discussion with Ralph Heichmeier, where we explore the surge in global defense spending and why defense investing is moving from the margins to the center of capital markets. Don't forget to subscribe to The Bit, wherever you get your podcasts.
turns.zh: 如果你喜欢这次对话，可以去听听我和 Rolf Heitmeyer 的讨论，在那里我们探讨了全球国防开支的激增，以及为什么国防投资正在从边缘走向资本市场的中心。别忘了在你收听播客的任何平台上订阅 The Bid。
